subject: RFI: commitment sizing & workload-to-GPU mapping for AuroraAI
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@auroraai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: AuroraAI Engineering <eng@auroraai.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: RFI: commitment sizing & workload-to-GPU mapping for AuroraAI

Connor — thanks for taking this. We're preparing an RFI to evaluate dedicated reservation options for our inference workloads running in EU. High-level asks:

- We need guidance mapping our real workload profile to a recommended GPU mix for a reserved pool (baseline + burst).
- Throughput targets: target sustained throughput of ~12M tokens/min during business hours with spikes to 25M tokens/min during peak batch windows.
- Latency SLO: P95 < 350ms for chat completions (avg prompt length ~450 tokens), some background batch jobs can tolerate 2–3s.

Attached is a small sample of our traces (aurora-workload-sample.csv). Can you fill your sizing template and recommend what reservation tiers (GPU types and counts) make sense for EU region? Also call out where we should consider KV/prefix cache and on-demand fallback.

Appreciate succinct recommendations — we have an internal procurement deadline next Thursday.

— Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Platform 
AuroraAI
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@auroraai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: commitment sizing & workload-to-GPU mapping for AuroraAI

Thanks Sam — great context. I've attached our Dedicated Sizing template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) to map your CSV traces to an expected GPU profile. Quick notes / assumptions before we fill it out:

- Workload mix: please confirm percent split between interactive chat (low latency) vs batched rerank/embeddings jobs — if not available, we'll assume 70/30 interactive/batch for initial sizing.
- Typical sequence lengths: you mentioned ~450 tokens for prompts; confirm whether that refers to prompt-only or total (prompt+response). We size GPU memory around peak total sequence length.
- Target concurrency: is the 12M tokens/min target measured across all models or a single primary model?
- Do you require strict data residency (EU-only) or would a multi-region fallback be acceptable for burst capacity?

If you can confirm those 3 items, Ben and Karthik and I will produce an initial recommendation and a few reservation scenarios (baseline, baseline+burst, and baseline+burst+on-demand). We'll call out expected cost delta for 3/6/12-month commits.

Proposed next step: 30-min sizing review on Tue or Wed — what works for you?

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@auroraai.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: AuroraAI Engineering <eng@auroraai.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: commitment sizing & workload-to-GPU mapping for AuroraAI

Connor — answers below:

- Workload split: 65% interactive chat (real-time assistants), 35% batch (rerank + nightly indexing).
- Sequence length: average prompt 350 tokens, expected average response 500 tokens (total ~850 tokens typical for chat). Some complex flows hit 1,500 tokens.
- Tokens/min: the 12M tokens/min target is across our entire fleet for EU. The primary model is a 70B decoder model (open-model family), but we also run a smaller 7B model for low-cost inference on low-complexity prompts.
- Residency: EU-only required for baseline; burst can fall back to our US region if needed but we'd prefer EU-localized burst if possible.

I've invited our infra lead to the sizing meeting if you can accommodate Tue 2026-06-15 10:00 CET. Also attaching a short doc with example traces and peak windows.

— Sam
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@auroraai.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: commitment sizing & workload-to-GPU mapping for AuroraAI

Sam — thanks for the details. We ran a quick mapping based on the profile you provided and here are three reservation scenarios (high level):

1) Conservative baseline (EU-only, 3-month commit)
- GPU mix: 6x A100-80GB (for 70B baseline serving) + 8x A10G (for 7B and background jobs)
- Expected sustained throughput: ~11–13M tokens/min (averaged)
- Peak headroom: ~1.5x with autoscaling burst to on-demand nodes
- Notes: good memory and batching for long sequences, KV cache recommended for repeated context; expect P95 ~300–380ms depending on prompt lengths.

2) Baseline + burst (preferred)
- GPU mix: 8x A100-80GB (baseline) + 12x A100-80GB reserved as burst pool (warm) + 10x A10G for smaller workloads
- Expected sustained throughput: 12–14M tokens/min baseline; burst capacity supports spikes to 26–28M tokens/min for <30 minute windows
- Cost recommendation: 6–8% incremental discount for burst-with-reservation vs pure on-demand.

3) Aggressive baseline (12-month commit, optimized cost)
- GPU mix: 10x H100-80GB (if you prefer higher single-request throughput and lower latency) + 8x A10G for low-cost paths
- Expected sustained throughput: 15–18M tokens/min, P95 < 250ms for typical chat flows with optimized batching and KV cache
- Notes: H100 provides better throughput per card but requires a higher commit and has different kernel/quantization implications. We'll include quantization guidance in the PDF.

Operational recommendations:
- KV/prefix caching: enable for interactive sessions where user context repeats (saves ~30–45% token compute for repeated turns).
- Batching window: tune to 8–12ms for chat to balance latency and token cost; allow larger windows for rerank jobs (50–100ms).
- Rollout: start with scenario #1 for procurement speed, then move to #2 after 3 months once workload patterns stabilize.

I've attached a short summary PDF (redwood-gpu-recommendation-summary.pdf) and populated the sizing template with numbers from your CSV. We'll bring a cost delta estimate to the Tue meeting.

Would you like us to include a fallback plan that routes lower-priority traffic to US region during major EU-wide spikes? We can diagram the routing policy and SLA implications.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@auroraai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: RFI: commitment sizing & workload-to-GPU mapping for AuroraAI

Sam — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. Tue 2026-06-15 10:00 CET works for the sizing review (we've confirmed Ben and Karthik will join). Action items before the call:

- Aurora to confirm the peak 30-minute window dates in the Drive doc (you already attached).
- Aurora to confirm whether the 70B model will be served in a quantized 4-bit profile or FP16; Ben, please include an estimated performance delta for both in the deck.
- Redwood to prepare routing policy options (EU-only baseline with US fallback) and a short slide on SLA/latency tradeoffs.
- Redwood to include SOC2 and data-residency notes in follow-up packet for procurement (Sam requested).

We'll share the populated sizing worksheet after the call with explicit GPU counts and monthly cost estimates for 3/6/12 month commit terms. Thanks — look forward to the meeting.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
